# Handoff: the Prepare header's ⋯ menu, two groups

Written 2026-10-27 for a coding agent on `jusprin-newui` (at e72f5b8070). Untracked working note: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Read `AGENTS.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching anything outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

## What was decided (Kenneth, 2026-10-27)

The "…" button at the right of the Prepare header keeps its glyph. Its menu becomes two groups separated by hairlines:

1. **This project:** a clickable project-name row, Version history, Export project 3MF…
2. **The app:** Preferences… (with ⌘, / Ctrl+,)
3. A hairline, then **Switch to classic view…** last.

Gone from the menu: the unclickable title row, Recent projects (its homes are Home's gallery and OrcaSlicer's File › Recent files), Back to Prepare (the Tab-key flip to OrcaSlicer's Preview is stopped at the shell instead). Not added: a gear glyph, Keyboard shortcuts, Report a problem (nothing in the app stands behind them).

Recent files, decided the same day: when JusPrin starts a project from a model file (STL/STEP/OBJ/…), that file's path is added to OrcaSlicer's File › Recent files through the existing `MainFrame::add_to_recent_projects`, regardless of the `recent_models` preference. A Recent entry must behave exactly like opening that file from the OS again.

The design is on the "JusPrin v2" canvas, https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, version `1793148288-e9fb`: board `main-10-prepare-header-project-menu` on the Main Page (under home-first-run) and the "In a project" stage of `prefs-13-entry-points` ("Where Preferences opens", Agent setup & Preferences page). The decision history is in `prepare-overflow-menu-proposal.md` beside this note.

## The menu as drawn

280 DIP popover (`component.popover.width`), rows 36 DIP, Body 14, on `surface.raised`; a separator is a 1 DIP `border.subtle` hairline inset to the row edges with 4 DIP above and below (what `HeaderMenu` already draws for `HeaderMenuItem::separator`).

| Row | Look | Press |
|---|---|---|
| Project name | Body Bold name, ellipsized; save-state word ("Saved", "Saving…", "Couldn't save", "Unsaved changes") as right-aligned Label meta; trailing chevron-right | Opens the Project tab of the Plates and Project pane, opening the pane first if it is collapsed |
| Version history | Body | The Project tab's Versions view |
| Export project 3MF… | Body | The same export the Project tab runs |
| hairline | | |
| Preferences… | Body, meta "⌘," on macOS / "Ctrl+," elsewhere | `wxGetApp().open_preferences()` as now |
| hairline | | |
| Switch to classic view… | Body | `detach_shell()` as now |

The two autosave warning rows ("Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry.", "Some older project data couldn't be removed.") keep their place directly under the name row, as disabled rows, exactly as `show_overflow_menu` inserts them today. The board does not draw them; the behaviour stays.

## Where the code is

Everything below is fork-owned. No OrcaSlicer-owned file should need to change; if one does, follow fork-stewardship.md and say so in the PR.

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp`, `StatusRow::show_overflow_menu()` builds the menu today (title row, Recent projects…, Back to Prepare, Preferences…, Switch to classic view…) and `show_recent_projects()` is the Recent list; both go. `project_summary()` stays: the button tooltip and four harness checks read it (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` 2449, 2522, 5625, 11057 compare `project_summary().BeforeFirst('\n')`); the new name row takes the name and the state word separately instead of the em-dash join.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.hpp`, `struct HeaderMenuItem`: `label`, `icon`, `detail` (right-aligned meta), `enabled`, `separator`, `invoke`, `title`, `keeps_open`, `decoration` (`HeaderRowDecoration`: `bold`, `trailing` icon, `detail`, …), `name`. A separator entry is `{}` with `separator = true` (see `PrinterMenu.cpp:18`). The name row is `decoration.bold = true`, `decoration.trailing = HeaderIcon::Right`, `detail` = the state word.
- `StatusRow` has no pointer to the pane. It gets callbacks from `ShellController` the way it gets `set_left_pane_toggle` (ShellController.cpp:650) and `set_agent_pane_toggle` (:319). Add one callback for the project rows, supplied by `ShellController`, that: expands the pane if `is_left_pane_collapsed()` (`toggle_left_pane()`), then calls `LeftPane::show_project()`, `LeftPane::open_project_view(ProjectView::Versions)` or `LeftPane::export_project()` (`Shell/LeftPane.hpp`, public). Do not reimplement export in the header; the pane's `export_project()` (`LeftPaneProject.cpp` ~148) is the one implementation.
- Back to Prepare: `StatusRow::request_prepare()` stays (slicing uses it); only the menu row goes. `ShellController.cpp:1526` picks "Back to Preview" for the printer panel's back label when the Preview tab is selected; once the Tab flip is stopped, check whether that branch is still reachable and leave a one-line comment either way.

### Stopping the Tab flip

`GLCanvas3D.cpp:3750` posts `EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB` on a plain Tab press over the canvas; `Plater.cpp:5185` (3D canvas) and `:5255` (preview canvas) bind it to `select_next_view_3D()`, which switches the Notebook page under the JusPrin header. The shell's `on_frame_char_hook` (`ShellController.cpp:1316`) handles only Ctrl+comma. Stop the flip in fork-owned code: bind the shell's own `EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB` handler on the 3D canvas's `wxGLCanvas` (`plater->get_view3D_canvas3D()->get_wxglcanvas()`) at install, without `Skip()` so OrcaSlicer's handler never runs (handlers bound later run first), and unbind it in `uninstall()` so the classic view gets Tab back. Alternatives need an OrcaSlicer edit; prefer the bind. Verify in the harness that posting `SimpleEvent(EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB)` to that canvas leaves `tp3DEditor` selected.

### Recent files

- `ShellController::take_opened_files` (`ShellController.cpp:896`) is the fork's "start a project from this file" path for model files (OS open, Home's Open…, drops on Home; a drop on the Prepare canvas adds and must not add to the list). After `add_dropped_files(again)` succeeds, call `wxGetApp().mainframe->add_to_recent_projects(from_path(file))` for each opened model file (skip `.zip`). OrcaSlicer's `add_to_recent_projects` (`MainFrame.cpp:4075`) already checks the file exists and persists the list.
- Open question, decide with Kenneth or leave out: Home's dropped files are written under `<temp>/JusPrin-dropped/<digest>/<name>` (`OrcaHomeBackend::open_dropped_files`, ~447). Adding those paths puts temp-folder entries in the list. Recommended: skip paths under that folder.
- A model-file Recent entry: `MainFrame::open_recent_project` (`MainFrame.cpp:4168`) calls `Plater::load_project(filename)`; `Plater::load_project` (`Plater.cpp:12164`) hands the path to the fork's `set_external_project_open_handler` (`ShellController.cpp:464`). That handler asks the "Previously opened file" question for any path, but an OS open of a model file never asks (`take_opened_files` does not consult `projects_for_source`). To keep "exactly like the OS", make the handler route a non-`.3mf` path to `take_opened_files({path})` and return its result; `.3mf` keeps the question. A missing file already gets OrcaSlicer's "The project is no longer available." dialog.
- Nothing else changes in OrcaSlicer's Recent files: no fork submenu, no path-to-project mapping, `recent_models` untouched.

## Tests, in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (target `shell_integration_harness`)

- `verify_header_overflow()` (~6826) currently asserts the menu keeps Recent projects… and has no Version history / Export rows; invert it to the new rows (by window name: `_L("Version history")`, `_L("Export project 3MF…")`, `_L("Preferences…")`, `_L("Switch to classic view…")`, the project name) and that Recent projects… and Back to Prepare are absent. Keep the existing `.3mf` reopen checks green.

# Prepare header: what the "…" menu holds and what it should hold

Written 2026-10-27 from the code on `jusprin-newui` (StatusRow.cpp, LeftPaneProject.cpp, PrinterMenu.cpp, FilamentMenu.cpp, ShellController.cpp, HomeUI App.tsx) and `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`. Untracked working note; not for commit.

## What the Prepare screen does

Prepare is the project window of the new shell. One header row sits across the top:

- Left: Home, and the toggle for the Plates and Project pane when that pane is closed.
- Centre: the printer-and-filament chip. Its printer half opens a menu (other printers, Printer settings…, Calibrate…, Add a printer…); its filament half opens the slot menu (filaments, colours, Use what's loaded on the printer…, Filament settings…, Calibrate this filament…).
- Right: the split print button (Slice / Print plate N, with Check Print, Print…, Print all plates…, Export sliced file… in its dropdown), the "…" overflow button, and the Agent-panel toggle.

Under the header: the Plates and Project pane on the left (plate rows with Rename, Arrange, Auto-orient, Lock, Plate settings…, Delete; + Add model, + Add plate; a Project tab with the project name and save state, Details, Version history, Export project 3MF…, Print history, Edit Project Info), the 3D canvas with the tool strip (Move, Rotate, Scale, Add instance, More = OrcaSlicer's right-click menu), and the Agent pane (chat, setup card, All settings, chat navigation, Preferences › Agent for setup).

OrcaSlicer's own menus stay on screen on every platform: the macOS menu bar (File, Edit, View, Window, Help) and, on Windows and Linux, OrcaSlicer's title bar with the same dropdowns plus Undo and Redo. The shell removes only the Calibration menu. So every OrcaSlicer command is still reachable, and the overflow menu does not need to carry them.

## The menu today

1. Project name with its save state ("Saved", "Saving…", "Couldn't save", "Unsaved changes"): a title row, not clickable. A warning row is added under it when autosave failed or old project data couldn't be removed.
2. Recent projects… (eight at a time, "Older projects…" pages on; opening one swaps the project in place)
3. Back to Prepare
4. Preferences… (⌘, / Ctrl+,)
5. Switch to classic view… (uninstalls the shell and shows stock OrcaSlicer)

What is wrong with it:

- The project name is a row you cannot click, and when the Plates and Project pane is closed it is the only place on Prepare that shows the name. The product definition says the name and save state are continuously visible, and that Project details opens "from the project name or menu". Neither holds today.
- "Back to Prepare" sits on the Prepare screen. It is there because Tab on the canvas still flips OrcaSlicer to its Preview tab under the JusPrin header (GLCanvas3D posts the tab event; the shell's key hook only handles Ctrl+,). Check print itself is a modal now, so the row is a repair for a leak, shown all the time.
- Four different scopes in one list: this project, navigation, the app, and an escape hatch.

With the RDP session **connected** (see [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]] for the disconnected case), native wx surfaces can be driven from PowerShell with `SetCursorPos` + `mouse_event` + `keybd_event` and captured with `Graphics.CopyFromScreen`. Worked on 2026-10-02 for the left pane (`shell_integration_harness --manual-left-pane`). Four traps, each of which first looked like a defect in the app:

- **Arrow keys need `KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY` (flag 1).** Without it `keybd_event(VK_DOWN)` arrives as `WXK_NUMPAD_DOWN` (379), not `WXK_DOWN` (317), so a handler testing only `WXK_DOWN` looks dead. (Real numpad arrows send the same code, so handlers should accept both.)
- **The GL canvas takes keyboard focus when the pointer enters it.** Parking the cursor over the canvas between a click and a key press moves focus off the control under test. Park it inside the surface being tested.
- **Coordinates are virtualized, the screen copy is not.** PowerShell is DPI-unaware: `GetWindowRect`/`SetCursorPos` use logical units (screen reads 1728x1084 at 200%), while `CopyFromScreen` wants real pixels. Multiply by `GetDeviceCaps(DESKTOPHORZRES=118) / GetDeviceCaps(HORZRES=8)`.
- **Tab is not available for focus traversal**: OrcaSlicer binds it to switching Prepare/Preview, and `wxWindow::Navigate()` is a no-op in this wx build (`wxHAS_NATIVE_TAB_TRAVERSAL`). Fork surfaces must move focus themselves (the left pane does it in a `wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK` handler).

**Why:** each cost a rebuild-and-retry loop before the cause turned out to be the instrument, not the code. Same lesson as [[verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app]].

**How to apply:** start from a scratch `ui.ps1` with Click-At / Press-Key / Capture helpers built on the rules above; when a key "does nothing", log the key code in the handler before changing the handler.

**Why:** This looks exactly like an application bug — gestures appear to have no effect and screenshots fail — so it can burn a long time before you realise the session, not the code, is the problem.

**How to apply:**
- Check `query session` first when input or capture stops working.
- Real UI testing still works without a desktop: `SendMessageTimeout` WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_MOUSEMOVE / WM_LBUTTONUP / WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK straight to the child HWND. This goes through the real wxMSW window procedure, real `SetCapture`, and real double-click handling — strictly more real than the harness's `ProcessEvent` injection, which bypasses `MSWWindowProc` entirely.
- A faithful drag must hold the pointer at a fixed **screen** x and recompute the client x from the target window's live `GetWindowRect` each step. Holding client x fixed makes a moving splitter run away, because the app converts with `ClientToScreen` against the window's current position.
- Screenshots still work disconnected through `PrintWindow(hwnd, hdc, 2)` (PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT): it draws the GL canvas and WebView2 panes (confirmed 2026-10-21). content.text:
I photographed the ⋯ menu in both themes. It matches the board in rows, colours, row size and width, but not in its hairlines. That mismatch comes from code every menu uses, not from this change. The 3× crops are above; the full window shots are in `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--src-JusPrin\78a54d34-2914-4799-bc78-ceca9b8b30f8\scratchpad\menu-shots-light\` and `…\menu-shots-dark\`.

**What matches the board**
- **Rows:** the project name in bold with the save state and a chevron on the right, then Version history, Export project 3MF…, a hairline, Preferences… with "Ctrl+,", a hairline, and Switch to classic view…. The board shows ⌘, and notes that Windows shows Ctrl+,.
- **Colours:** I measured the pixels. The menu's background, outline and main text are exactly the token colours in both themes. The plain rows look heavier than you might expect on Windows, but they are drawn in the regular Body font and only the name is bold, as on the board.
- **Size:** rows are 36 DIP tall, 2 DIP apart, with 8 DIP of padding at the top and bottom. The menu is 280 DIP wide and its right edge lines up with the ⋯ button.

**What doesn't match**
- **The hairlines are wrong in both themes.**
  - **Colour:** they are mid-grey (#A0A0A0) instead of the subtle border colour. In dark mode that grey is much brighter than the rest of the menu.
  - **Length:** they run edge to edge, where the board stops them 12 DIP short of each side.
  - **Thickness:** in dark mode they are 2 pixels thick.
  - **Cause:** the menu draws each line with a standard Windows line control, which ignores the colour it is given. The plate and object menus show the same grey line, so this was already there before the menu work. I haven't checked it on macOS.
- **Small differences, also from the shared menu code:**
  - **Position:** the menu opens about 5 DIP below the ⋯ button, overlapping the bottom of the header. The board puts it 4 DIP below the header.
  - **Shadow:** the menu has no drop shadow. The board has a medium shadow.
  - **Around the hairlines:** the board leaves 13 DIP; the app leaves 9 DIP.

**Harness change:** to take the pictures I added a menu shot to the `--left-pane-capture` run in [shell_harness.cpp](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp). It only runs when that mode is given a folder. Both the light and the dark run passed with no failures. I deleted their WebView2 folders, and nothing is committed.

content.text:
The marks were 18 pixels of full-strength button colour on the top and bottom edges where the two halves of the Slice button meet. They're gone now in both light and dark.

**Cause** ([HeaderControls.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp)): each half of the button is drawn as a rounded rectangle, and then a small square patch is painted over the inner corners to make them straight where the halves meet.
- **The rounded rectangle** is drawn half a pixel in, so its top and bottom pixel rows are only half filled. That gives a soft edge (#724B6B in dark).
- **The square patch** starts on whole pixels, so it fills those rows completely (#CE84B7).
- **Result:** where the patches sit, on both sides of the split, the edge turns into a short, harder line. In dark mode it is brighter than the rest of the edge, and in light mode darker.

**Fix:** I removed the patch. Each half now draws its rounded rectangle extended past the split, so its inner corners fall outside the button and are never drawn. The printer chip next to it already works this way.
- With the extension at one corner's width, the curve started right at the split, which left 2 slightly lighter pixels on the top edge. Extending by twice that width cleared them.
- **Measured in fresh captures:** the top and bottom rows are now one even colour end to end in both themes. The outer rounded corners are pixel-for-pixel unchanged.

**Tests:** both theme captures passed with no failures. The full default harness shows only the six known Windows failures.
